project.name: plumb-engine
project.description:
LAYER 2 -- the analysis engine. Everything that turns source into findings lives here:
- plumb-tac the language-neutral TAC IR, its builder, the Java AST translator and the Jimple (bytecode) translator. - plumb-frontend the non-Java source frontends: Kotlin (Analysis API Standalone) and Scala 3 (dotc PluginPhase). - plumb-dfa the dataflow engine: call graph, taint, the checkers and the YAML rule/sink-family configuration. - plumb-style the structural and style checkers. - plumb-dsl-kotlin the Kotlin rule DSL. - plumb-ai the LLM agent layer over the analysis results.
THE IR IS THE SEAM BETWEEN THE FRONTENDS AND THE ANALYSIS. Every frontend lowers to the same TAC, so the DFA never learns about Kotlin or Scala; and every language-specific behaviour is expressed by the frontend's degradation (a construct becomes BRANCH/CALL/MOVE) and by a rule's language binding, never by a new opcode.
plumb-frontend is SEPARATE from plumb-tac on purpose. It depends on a compiler's API rather than on a stable published interface -- the Kotlin Analysis API (experimental) and dotc's PluginPhase (compiler-internal). A breaking upstream change in either must not be able to break the Java analysis path, so neither may live in plumb-tac.
